They may push rows into `floor` or `indeterminate` and away from the comparable set, or make the engines judge the plan as having unbacked citations.

scenarios: A plan citing `[rebar:X]` gets item-9 or edge-check findings it did not get historically.
Several of only 11 rows become floor-blocked, leaving few comparable items.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write `--out` atomically (temp file + os.replace), and have `--resume` refuse to proceed when the recorded corpus digest differs from the current selection.
evidence: "`--out` is rewritten after every item. `--resume` skips rows whose `review_event_uuid` is already recorded with no `error` on either engine."
findings.finding: Checkpointing rewrites `--out` after every item during a run of about 4 hours, but the plan does not require an atomic write. `--resume` also does not check that the recorded corpus digest matches the current labels and `--limit` selection, so a resumed run could silently mix corpora.
findings.location: Approach → Checkpointing
scenarios: A crash or Ctrl-C mid-write leaves truncated JSON, and `--resume` fails or restarts the whole run.
Resuming with a different `--labels` merges items from two corpora under one digest.
findings.suggested_fix: Write to `<out>.tmp`, then `os.replace(tmp, out)`. On `--resume`, load the existing file and abort with a clear error if `existing['corpus_digest'] != current_digest`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and justify the fixture ref and store contents (HEAD vs the row's historical review ref; file_impact-only vs fuller tree), and record the store-fidelity caveat alongside `historical_pipeline_verdict` in the results JSON.
evidence: "the fixture files are each `file_impact` path's content at the harness checkout's HEAD (`git show HEAD:<path>`; missing paths are skipped and counted)"
"Every file and ticket tool, in both engines, therefore reads the disposable store, never the real rebar repo or its ticket history"
"It is labelled `historical_pipeline_verdict`, not gold: it came from an older pipeline" — this names the pipeline drift but not the codebase or context drift
findings.finding: The fixture store holds only the `file_impact` paths, taken at today's HEAD, not at the ref each plan was historically reviewed against. Two effects follow. (a) Files a plan proposes to create, or that were since implemented, now exist with their post-implementation content. (b) Every non-file_impact path is absent: callers, tests, docs, and the tickets that plans cite. So code-grounding probes in both engines, especially the agentic engine's exploration, run against a context unlike the one either engine would see in production or saw historically. The plan does not acknowledge this. That undermines the 'historical_pipeline_verdict' comparison and makes some engine findings store artifacts.
findings.location: Approach → Per item ('content at the harness checkout's HEAD (`git show HEAD:<path>`)'); Report → historical agreement
scenarios: A row whose plan creates `foo.py`: at HEAD `foo.py` exists with the shipped implementation, so either engine may flag the capability as already existing and BLOCK where the historical review PASSed.
The agentic engine searches for callers or tests of a touched module. Nothing outside file_impact exists, so it reports false absence findings and inflates agentic-only overlap counts.
Plans citing other tickets (e.g. `[rebar:...]`) reference tickets the disposable store does not contain.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify an atomic `--out` write (temp + rename). Make `--resume` refuse on a digest/labels/threshold mismatch and replace (not duplicate) the records of errored rows it re-runs.
evidence: "`--out` is rewritten after every item."
"`--resume` skips rows whose `review_event_uuid` is already recorded with no `error` on either engine."
findings.finding: The checkpoint/resume lifecycle for the `--out` file is under-specified in two ways. (a) The file is 'rewritten after every item' with no atomic write (temp file + rename), so a crash or Ctrl-C mid-write during the 4-hour run can leave a truncated JSON that `--resume` cannot load. (b) `--resume` does not check that the existing file's corpus digest, labels file, `--limit` and `MATCH_THRESHOLD` match the current invocation. It also does not say how errored rows are replaced versus appended. A resumed run can therefore silently mix records from different corpora or thresholds into one 'recorded run'.
findings.location: Approach → Checkpointing
scenarios: An interrupt hits during the rewrite after item 9 of 11. The out file is partial JSON, `--resume` raises, and hours of live calls are lost.
The operator resumes with a different `--labels` or `--limit`. Old records are kept and merged under the new digest, and the committed results misreport their corpus.
findings.suggested_fix: Write to `<out>.tmp` and `os.replace` it. On `--resume`, load the file, assert that `digest` and `threshold` equal the current values, else exit non-zero. Key records by `review_event_uuid` so re-run rows overwrite their prior record.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Seed a fresh, identically populated `case_store` for EACH engine (or show that the agentic tools cannot read `.rebar/cache`), and add a test asserting that one engine's store artifacts are not visible to the other
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:32-37: `_checkpoint_dir` = Path(ctx.repo_root)/'.rebar'/'cache'/'plan-review'/ctx.ticket_id
Plan: 'Every file and ticket tool, in both engines, therefore reads the disposable store, never the real rebar repo' (isolation from the checkout only, not between the two engines)
The landed engine_comparison.py:265-276 reviews each engine in its OWN store specifically because 'the pipeline's Pass-1 checkpoints under .rebar/cache' would otherwise be visible to the other engine
findings.finding: The plan runs both engines on the same ticket in ONE disposable store, one after the other. It argues isolation only against the real repo and ticket history, and says only that no attestation or sidecar is written. But the pipeline engine writes Pass-1 checkpoint envelopes under `<repo_root>/.rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket_id>/`, which sign=False and emit_sidecar=False do not suppress. So the agentic engine, run second in the same store, may be able to read the pipeline's findings through its file tools, which would contaminate the overlap and agreement measures.
findings.location: Approach → Per item ('Inside `eval_solver.case_store(...)` ... for `e` in ("pipeline", "agentic")'); Testing ('No attestation or sidecar is written in the disposable store')
scenarios: The pipeline runs first and writes its Pass-1 findings to .rebar/cache; the agentic agent lists or greps the store, reads them, and echoes them, which inflates the matched count and agreement
findings.suggested_fix: For each engine, open its own `eval_solver.case_store({"files": files})`, create the ticket, set file_impact, and build cfg/runner rooted at that store before calling review_plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State where the disposable ticket's title comes from (the labels file has none; `create_ticket` requires one), e.g. the original ticket's title from the checkout tracker, falling back to the description's first prose line, and record the chosen title in each item record
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:123-125: create_ticket(ticket_type: str, title: str, *, ...): title is required
Searching the labels JSONL for '"title":' returned no matches; the plan lists the row fields as description, ticket_type, file_impact, children and verdict
The landed engine_comparison.py adds row_title(), which looks up the original ticket in the checkout tracker and falls back to the plan's first prose line, a design choice the plan never states
findings.finding: The plan says the harness 'creates one ticket of the row's `ticket_type` with the row's `description`', but `rebar.create_ticket` requires a positional `title`, and the replay label rows have no title field. The plan never says where the title comes from. Both engines review the title, so it is part of the reviewed material and should be pinned.
findings.location: Approach → Per item ('The harness creates one ticket of the row's `ticket_type` with the row's `description`')
scenarios: An implementer passes an empty or placeholder title, which may trip the DET floor or change what either engine reviews
The title is taken from the live tracker and can drift from the frozen corpus between runs

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Review each engine in its own identically-seeded case_store (same fixture files, same ticket), so nothing the pipeline writes (e.g. .rebar/cache/plan-review checkpoints) is visible to the agentic engine's tools, and add a test asserting the two reviews use different store roots.
evidence: Plan: one case_store per item, then review_plan for e in ("pipeline", "agentic")
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:32-37: _checkpoint_dir = Path(ctx.repo_root)/.rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket_id>
Plan Testing: 'No attestation or sidecar is written in the disposable store' — does not cover the checkpoint cache
findings.finding: Both engines review the same ticket in ONE disposable store, pipeline first. The pipeline's Pass-1 checkpointing writes reusable finding envelopes under <store>/.rebar/cache/plan-review/<tid>, so when the agentic engine runs next, its filesystem tools may read the pipeline's results. The plan's isolation claim only covers the real repo, and its test only checks that no attestation or sidecar is written. Checkpoints are neither, so that test does not catch this.
findings.location: Approach → Per item ("Inside eval_solver.case_store(...) ... for e in ("pipeline", "agentic")"); Testing last bullet
scenarios: The agentic engine greps or reads the store tree and finds the pipeline's Pass-1 findings for the same ticket, which inflates overlap and agreement.
A retry after a pipeline error reuses partial checkpoints. That is harmless for the pipeline, but the cached files are still visible to the agentic engine.
findings.suggested_fix: For each row, enter eval_solver.case_store({"files": files}) once per engine, recreate the ticket and file_impact inside it, and root cfg and runner at that store. Note the cost (one extra small git init per engine per row) in the Approach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either seed each store with the full HEAD tree (e.g. `git archive HEAD` extracted into the store) so both engines see the real repo with only the ticket store isolated, or state the positive rationale for file_impact-only seeding and record per item which referenced paths were absent.
evidence: Plan: fixture = file_impact paths only, via git show HEAD:<path>
Labels row 3 cites `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` and row 10 cites `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md`; their file_impact lists are narrower than the files the plans reference
No sentence in the plan explains why file_impact-only is the right fixture scope
findings.finding: The disposable store is seeded only with each row's file_impact paths. The agentic engine works by exploring the repository, and these plans cite files outside their file_impact (CI workflow files, docs, sibling modules). In the store those files are missing for both engines, so the harness measures the engines on a stripped-down repo, which hits the agentic engine harder. The plan gives no reason for limiting the fixture to file_impact.
findings.location: Approach → Per item ("the fixture files are each file_impact path's content at the harness checkout's HEAD ... missing paths are skipped and counted")
scenarios: The agentic engine opens a referenced module that is absent from the store and reports a 'file does not exist' finding. That finding shows up as agentic-only overlap or a blocking flip that does not reflect real engine behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the disposable ticket's title source (e.g. the original ticket's title read from the harness checkout's tracker by the row's ticket_id, falling back to the plan's first prose line) and record it per item.
evidence: Plan Context lists the row fields: description, ticket_type, file_impact, children, verdict — no title
Plan Approach never specifies the created ticket's title
findings.finding: The labels rows carry description, ticket_type and file_impact but no title, and the plan does not say what title the disposable ticket gets. Creating a ticket requires a title, and the title is part of the material both engines review. An arbitrary placeholder could cause title/description-mismatch findings that are artifacts of the harness.
findings.location: Approach → Per item ("creates one ticket of the row's ticket_type with the row's description")
scenarios: The implementer uses a generic title like 'plan <id>', and both engines flag the title as not matching the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] On --resume, refuse (or ignore the prior records) unless the existing file's corpus label file name and match_threshold equal the current run's, and test the mismatch case.
evidence: Plan: '--resume skips rows whose review_event_uuid is already recorded with no error on either engine.'
The plan defines a corpus digest but never checks it on resume
findings.finding: --resume skips any recorded row with no error on either engine, but it does not check that the existing --out file came from the same corpus. Records from an earlier run with a different --labels file, a different --limit, or another match threshold or code revision would be silently merged into a result whose corpus_digest describes the current selection.
findings.location: Approach → Checkpointing
scenarios: The operator runs --limit 3, then resumes with the full corpus and a different labels file, and gets a mixed record set under one digest.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say which verdict arrays feed the overlap (blocking + advisory + overflow, and whether `indeterminate[]` counts on a fail-open PASS), so the advisory cap does not cut off the counts.
evidence: Plan: "over each verdict's `blocking` + `advisory` with `tier != \"DET\"`"
plan_review_verdict.schema.json:23 advisory: "capped at the config top-N by priority. Overflow goes to the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar"; :36-38 `overflow`: "Advisory findings beyond the cap"
orchestrator.py:386-394: verify_failed with no blocking-criterion finding gives PASS, with the preserved findings in `indeterminate`
agentic_verdict.py:10: "Agentic findings carry no priority ... the stable advisory sort keeps the agent's order"; both engines go through partition_findings(advisory_cap=DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CAP)
findings.finding: Overlap is computed only over each verdict's `blocking` + `advisory`. In the verdict contract `advisory` is capped at the top-N, with the rest moved to `overflow[]`. On a verify_failed run that falls open to PASS, the pipeline's LLM findings sit in `indeterminate[]`. The plan never says whether these arrays count, so matched, pipeline-only and agentic-only counts are cut off by the cap, and the cut is uneven: the pipeline sorts by priority, while agentic findings have no priority and keep the agent's order.
findings.location: Approach → Report → Finding overlap
scenarios: An engine produces more advisory findings than the cap: the extra findings are invisible to overlap and counted as missing from that engine
The pipeline's verify step fails open to PASS: the row is scored, but all its pipeline LLM findings are skipped, so every agentic finding counts as agentic-only
findings.suggested_fix: Compute overlap over `blocking + advisory + overflow` with tier != DET, and either include `indeterminate[]` or record a per-item flag when a scored verdict carries LLM findings only in `indeterminate[]`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the two engines' `finding` text is made comparable (the agentic `title: description` composition against the pipeline's single sentence), and add a test fixture shaped like real agentic output, not only near-identical strings.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/agentic_verdict.py:35-41: text = f"{title}: {description}" ... "finding": text
Plan: "on the token sets of each finding's `finding` text (`sidecar._norm_tokens(f[\"finding\"]).split()`) with similarity ≥ `MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.5`"
Plan Testing: "pipeline findings {A, B, C} and agentic {A′, B′, D} (A′/B′ near-identical)"
findings.finding: The overlap rule treats each finding's `finding` text as comparable across engines, but the two engines build that field differently. The agentic adapter sets `finding` to `f"{title}: {description}"`, while pipeline findings carry one finding sentence. Token-set Jaccard ≥ 0.5 is sensitive to this length difference. The plan's only check is the A′/B′ 'near-identical' test case, which does not reflect the real field shapes.
findings.location: Approach → Report → Finding overlap; Testing → overlap worked example
scenarios: Both engines flag the same defect, but the agentic text adds a long description, so Jaccard falls below 0.5 and the pair counts as one pipeline-only plus one agentic-only finding

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that all 11 rows in the labels file are `verified` (or give the verified count) and make AC2's expected item count match the filter's output.
evidence: "keeping only `verified` rows"
"assert len(d['items'])==11"
"It holds 11 real rebar plans"
findings.finding: The corpus keeps only `verified` rows, yet AC2 hard-codes `len(d['items'])==11`, the plan says it runs over all 11 rows, and the Context says the file holds 11 plans. If any row is unverified, the filter yields fewer than 11 items and the AC cannot pass. Alternatively, the filter is a no-op that the plan never confirms.
findings.location: Approach → Corpus vs Acceptance Criteria (AC2) and Output ('over all 11 rows')
scenarios: One row has verified=false, so the harness emits 10 items and AC2 fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Context: 'all 11 rows are verified=true'. Or assert `len(d['items']) == d['corpus']['selected_count']` instead of the literal 11.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether `--limit N` returns exactly N rows (BLOCK rows displacing others) or first-N ∪ all-BLOCK rows, and assert the resulting row count in the test.
evidence: "`--limit N` keeps the first N in that order but always includes every recorded BLOCK row"
findings.finding: `--limit N` semantics are ambiguous about cardinality. 'keeps the first N … but always includes every recorded BLOCK row' implies a union that can exceed N (with 3 BLOCK rows, `--limit 1` may yield up to 4 rows). The test only checks that the BLOCK row is present, not the resulting count.
findings.location: Approach → Corpus; Testing ('`--limit 1` over rows with one BLOCK keeps that BLOCK row')
scenarios: One implementation returns N rows with BLOCK rows swapped in, another returns N + extra BLOCK rows. Both pass the test.
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'selected = first N rows ∪ all BLOCK rows, re-sorted by review_event_ts; length may exceed N'. In the test, assert `len(selected) == 2` for `--limit 1` with one non-first BLOCK row.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a calibration step: record the per-item similarity matrix (or the best-match score per finding) in the results, and report matched counts at several thresholds (e.g. 0.3/0.5/0.7) so the 0.5 choice is visibly justified.
evidence: "with similarity ≥ `MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.5`. The threshold is a module constant recorded in the results, not a config key."
The test uses a synthetic 'A′/B′ near-identical' pair, which does not exercise real cross-engine phrasing.
findings.finding: The finding-overlap match threshold (Jaccard ≥ 0.5 over normalized tokens) is asserted, not derived. The two engines phrase findings differently: pipeline rubric-shaped text versus free-form agent text. Lexical Jaccard may systematically undercount semantically identical findings, and the plan has no calibration or sensitivity step.
findings.location: Report → Finding overlap (`MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.5`)
scenarios: The live run reports near-zero matched findings because paraphrases score 0.2 to 0.4, and the epic concludes the engines disagree on findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Store each finding's best cross-engine similarity score in the per-item record, and add `overlap_by_threshold` for {0.3, 0.5, 0.7} to the summary.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either promote `_norm_tokens` to a public helper (or re-export it) or note the deliberate dependency, and pin the tokenization behavior in the unit test.
evidence: "`sidecar._norm_tokens(f["finding"]).split()`"
findings.finding: The overlap matcher imports a private helper from another module (`sidecar._norm_tokens`), coupling the eval harness to an underscore-prefixed internal of the sidecar module without acknowledgment.
findings.location: Report → Finding overlap
scenarios: A sidecar refactor renames or changes `_norm_tokens`, silently changing overlap results or breaking the harness.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the retry delay an injectable parameter (or monkeypatched `time.sleep`), and state that the unit test runs with zero delay.
evidence: "A retryable class (WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW) is retried once after 60 s before it is recorded."
findings.finding: The retry path sleeps 60 s before retrying a retryable error class, and Testing exercises exactly that path ('WAIT_AND_RETRY twice … retried once'). The plan does not make the sleep injectable, so the offline unit test would block for 60 s or more.
findings.location: Approach → Per-engine outcome (step 1); Testing (error bullet)
scenarios: `make verify` slows by a minute per retry test, or the test is skipped or flaky under timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `retry_delay_s: float = 60.0` argument to the per-item runner, and pass 0 from the test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per arm, the disposition: budget exhaustion → `error` (retryable or not) or `indeterminate` (permanent); which attempt's class is recorded after a failed retry; and the non-zero exit code for an invalid run.
evidence: "an outage, refusal, auth/config fault or agent budget exhaustion degrades to an unsigned INDETERMINATE"
"`error`: a raised exception, or an INDETERMINATE whose coverage has `llm_unavailable`, `input_rejected` or `config_fault`"
"A retryable class (WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW) is retried once after 60 s before it is recorded."
No exit-code statement for `"valid": false`
findings.finding: The failure-disposition contract is incomplete. (a) The plan lists 'agent budget exhaustion' among the cases that degrade to an unsigned INDETERMINATE but never maps it to an outcome. Unless it carries `llm_unavailable`/`input_rejected`/`config_fault`, it falls into `indeterminate`: it is never retried, and `--resume` will skip it as non-error, so it is treated as a permanent outcome without the plan saying so. (b) It does not state which class is recorded when the single retry also fails (first vs second attempt). (c) It does not state the CLI exit status for an invalid run, or for a run containing errors, so the operator cannot tell a degraded run from a clean one by exit code.
findings.location: Approach → Per-engine outcome (steps 1–3 and the 'valid: false' rule)
scenarios: The agentic engine exhausts its budget on a large plan. The row records `indeterminate`, so it is excluded from agreement and never re-run by `--resume`, and the run looks clean.
An all-error engine produces `valid: false`, but the CLI exits 0 and an operator commits the results.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach → Report, either reuse `rebar.llm.parity` (ItemRecord / parity_report metrics) for agreement and flips, or add one sentence saying why not (e.g. a descriptive comparison rather than a gate, 11 items is below MIN_GOLD_ITEMS, a four-way outcome taxonomy) and that its numbers are not comparable with provider_parity's.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/parity.py:70-80: verdict_decision is "the two-bucket mapping every harness scored against parity_report must use, so their recorded evidence stays comparable"
src/rebar/llm/parity.py:134-235: parity_report computes verdict_agreement, decision_flips and errored_pairs from paired records
src/rebar/llm/parity.py:367-383: parallel_run_and_diff runs both arms over a corpus and pairs the records
src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:1-30, 253-260: operator-run two-arm harness with corpus_digest and committed results
Absence: the plan never mentions rebar.llm.parity or explains its own agreement/flip definitions against it
findings.finding: The plan builds its own agreement, flip and error-exclusion report without mentioning the repo's existing two-arm comparison toolkit or explaining why it doesn't reuse it. `rebar.llm.parity` already provides `ItemRecord`, `verdict_decision`, `parity_report` (agreement, decision flips, errored pairs excluded and reported) and `parallel_run_and_diff` (paired live driver). Its docstring says every harness scored against it must use the same verdict_decision mapping so recorded evidence stays comparable. `provider_parity` is a sibling operator-run harness with the same corpus_digest and committed-results shape. The plan borrows `classify_error` from provider_parity, so the authors know it exists, but never says whether the engine comparison reuses or deliberately diverges from parity.py.
findings.location: Approach → Report; Approach → Corpus (digest)
scenarios: A reader puts the engine-comparison agreement next to provider-parity agreement and assumes they mean the same thing. They don't: parity_report counts gold-improving flips as agreement, while this harness counts any disagreement.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Report → Finding overlap, cite `plan_replay/tier2.finding_set_comparison` and state why the harness uses greedy token-Jaccard pairing instead (cross-engine rewording defeats exact `norm_id`), plus where the 0.5 threshold comes from (e.g. hand-checked on a sample of pairs).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py:436-460: finding_set_comparison, DET-excluded Jaccard over norm_id with per-criterion gained/lost/unchanged
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py:229: an existing _jaccard helper
Plan: "Pairs are matched greedily, highest Jaccard similarity first ... with similarity ≥ `MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.5`"
Absence: no reference to tier2's comparison and no reason given for the 0.5 threshold
findings.finding: The finding-overlap metric adds a second, differently defined comparison without reference to the one already in the repo. `plan_replay/tier2.finding_set_comparison` already compares two finding sets with DET findings excluded, using whole-set Jaccard over `sidecar.norm_id` plus per-criterion gained/lost counts. The plan introduces greedy pairwise token-Jaccard matching at a 0.5 threshold, with DET exclusion by `tier` rather than by criterion. Fuzzy matching is probably justified, since exact norm_id would almost never match across engines that word findings differently. But the plan doesn't state that reason, doesn't mention the existing metric, and gives no basis for choosing 0.5.
findings.location: Approach → Report → Finding overlap
scenarios: Someone later compares the engine-overlap numbers with a Tier-2 replay's jaccard_mean and reads them as the same measure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach → Per item, say how the model chain is pinned (e.g. an empty-fallback `[llm.model_classes]` config root like `plan_replay/parity`, adapted for the Anthropic API) or explicitly accept the confound, and record the resolved model per engine call in the results JSON.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py:1-10: "evaluating a change on a different model than production runs confounds the measurement, and PydanticAIRunner.run re-derives its fallback chain from the resolved model string and cfg.repo_path on every call"
Plan: "`runner` is `get_runner(cfg)` ... while the production model classes still apply"
Provenance: "via the Anthropic API during the Bedrock spend-cap deny"; parity.py:40-43 requires a bedrock: model
findings.finding: The plan doesn't consider the repo's model-parity guard. `plan_replay/parity.resolve_pinned_model` exists because `PydanticAIRunner.run` re-derives a fallback chain from the model string and `cfg.repo_path` on every call, and a fallback to another model confounds an eval measurement. The plan uses `get_runner(cfg)` with the operator's `resolve_gate_config()` and `repo_path=store`. So which fallback chain applies, and whether one engine can silently fall back to a different model mid-run, are both unspecified. The recorded results don't capture the model actually used per call. resolve_pinned_model only accepts Bedrock, and the provenance says the run goes through the Anthropic API during a Bedrock spend-cap deny, so the plan has to say explicitly how it pins models or accepts the confound.
findings.location: Approach → Per item (`cfg` / `runner`); Acceptance Criteria → provenance
scenarios: During the ~4 h run the agentic engine hits throttling and falls back to a different model class on some items while the pipeline doesn't. The recorded agreement then partly reflects the model difference, not the engines.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add Cohen's kappa (computed from the existing 2×2 matrix) next to raw agreement in the summary, or note in the epic comment that raw agreement isn't chance-corrected given the PASS-heavy corpus.
evidence: Plan: "Agreement counts only items where both engines produced PASS/BLOCK" — raw proportion only
Context: corpus is "7 PASS, 3 BLOCK, 1 INDETERMINATE"
findings.finding: The report gives only raw percent agreement on a skewed corpus (7 PASS / 3 BLOCK historically, with roughly 8 or fewer scorable items). It doesn't consider the standard chance-corrected two-rater statistic, Cohen's kappa. When one category dominates, raw agreement overstates how far two raters really agree. The 2×2 matrix is recorded, so kappa can be derived, but the summary on the epic will quote a raw figure.
findings.location: Approach → Report (Agreement; 2×2 confusion matrix)
scenarios: Both engines PASS most items because most plans are fine, and the epic summary reports high agreement that reflects the base rate rather than engines making the same decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute kappa = (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e) from the 2×2 matrix, with p_e = sum over {PASS, BLOCK} of (pipeline marginal × agentic marginal) / n². Report null when p_e == 1, and pin it in the existing agreement test.

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)
